mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where this trigger occurs, or the effect reverses during a financial crisis.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of 2% or more signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during a supply-chain shock.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered periods, or the effect is reversed during a fiscal stimulus rollout.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of 1% or more for four consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by ≥1% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during a global supply shock.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening in monetary and price pressures, which increases risk aversion and yields, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed their 12-month moving averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of co-triggered months, or the effect is reversed during a financial crisis.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by at least 1% signals a broad-based collapse in demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both fall by ≥1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of co-triggered months, or the effect is absent during a supply-side shock.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average combined with a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals an overheating labor market, which increases wage pressures and inflation risk, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days in a low-inflation regime.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-mo MA and UNRATE < 4% in the same month, with CPIAUCSL < 2.5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of co-triggered months under the specified regime, or the effect reverses when inflation spikes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) of at least 0.5% for six consecutive months signals a robust manufacturing expansion, which boosts earnings for industrial firms and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered months, or the effect disappears during a global supply shock.
